MARCUS T. WILLIAMS

                                  Senior Data Scientist

Address: 2847 Columbia Pike, Apt 412        Phone: (703) 555-8294
Arlington, VA 22204                         Email: marcus.williams@email.com
Citizenship: United States                   Clearance: Top Secret/SCI (Active)
Veteran Status: N/A                       Federal Status: GS-14, Step 7



PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

Senior Data Scientist with 12 years of progressive federal experience in statistical modeling, machine
learning, and cybersecurity analytics. Demonstrated expertise in designing and deploying large-
scale data infrastructure supporting national security missions. Proven track record of leading cross-
agency analytical initiatives, mentoring junior data scientists, and translating complex analytical
ﬁndings into actionable intelligence for senior leadership. Skilled in Python, R, Spark, and cloud-
based ML platforms with extensive experience processing classiﬁed datasets at scale. Holds active
Top Secret/SCI clearance with CI polygraph.

WORK EXPERIENCE

Senior Data Scientist (Lead)

Grade/Series: GS-14/1560                Hours per Week: 40
Salary: $138,491 per annum                  Dates: 03/2021 – Present
Employer: Department of Homeland Security, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
(CISA)
Address: 245 Murray Lane SW, Washington, DC 20528
Supervisor: Dr. Angela Richardson, (202) 555-4173 (may be contacted)

• Serve as technical lead for the Threat Analytics Division, directing a team of 8 data scientists
   and 4 data engineers in developing machine learning models that process 2.3 billion network
   events daily from federal civilian agency (.gov) networks

• Architected and deployed the Automated Indicator Sharing (AIS) anomaly detection platform
   using ensemble methods (Random Forest, XGBoost, deep autoencoders), reducing mean time
   to detect advanced persistent threats from 78 days to 11 days across 102 federal agencies

• Designed and implemented a graph neural network (GNN) pipeline for lateral movement de-
    tection, achieving 94.2% precision and 91.7% recall on classiﬁed validation datasets, directly
   contributing to the identiﬁcation of 3 nation-state intrusion campaigns in FY2023

• Led the migration of legacy analytics infrastructure from on-premises Hadoop clusters to AWS
   GovCloud (IL-5), reducing compute costs by 34% ($2.1M annual savings) while increasing
   processing throughput by 4.7x

• Developed Natural Language Processing models for automated analysis of 450,000+ vulnera-
    bility disclosures annually, enabling prioritized patch guidance to critical infrastructure sectors
   within 48 hours of disclosure

• Authored 14 technical white papers and Intelligence Community Directives (ICDs) establishing
   data science standards and best practices for cyber threat intelligence analytics across DHS
   component agencies

• Represented CISA at the National Security Council’s Cyber Directorate, providing technical

Marcus T. Williams                                                         Page 2



   brieﬁngs on AI/ML capabilities for national cyber defense to senior government oﬃcials includ-
   ing the National Cyber Director

• Established and chair the DHS Data Science Working Group (47 members across 6 compo-
   nent agencies), driving standardization of ML model governance, bias testing, and deployment
   protocols

• Mentored 6 junior data scientists (GS-9 through GS-12) through the CISA Data Science Devel-
   opment Program, with 4 achieving promotion within 18 months

• Developed an insider threat behavioral analytics model integrating 23 data sources (badge
    access, network logs, email metadata, ﬁnancial disclosures) achieving AUC of 0.96, adopted by
   3 additional federal agencies

• Coordinated with NSA, FBI Cyber Division, and US-CERT on joint analytical products, au-
   thoring 8 Joint Analysis Reports (JARs) disseminated to critical infrastructure owners and
   operators

• Implemented MLOps pipelines using Kubeﬂow on classiﬁed infrastructure, reducing model de-
   ployment time from 6 weeks to 3 days and enabling continuous model retraining on streaming
   threat data

• Presented research ﬁndings at classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed venues including the NSA Cybersecurity
   Symposium, the DHS Science and Technology Conference, and the Intelligence Community Data
   Science Summit

Data Scientist

Grade/Series: GS-13/1560                Hours per Week: 40
Salary: $112,890 per annum                  Dates: 06/2017 – 02/2021
Employer: National Security Agency (NSA), Cybersecurity Directorate
Address: 9800 Savage Road, Fort Meade, MD 20755
Supervisor: James K. Okonkwo, (301) 555-6241 (may be contacted with advance notice)

• Developed and deployed deep learning models for encrypted traﬃc classiﬁcation, enabling iden-
   tiﬁcation of malicious command-and-control communications with 97.3% accuracy without de-
   cryption, processing 800TB of network metadata daily

• Built scalable feature engineering pipelines using Apache Spark and custom Python libraries,
   transforming raw SIGINT data into structured analytical products consumed by 200+ intelli-
   gence analysts across the IC

• Designed Bayesian network models for attribution analysis, providing probabilistic assessments
    of threat actor identity that directly supported 5 National Intelligence Estimates (NIEs) pre-
   sented to the President’s Daily Brief

• Led a 4-person team in developing time-series anomaly detection algorithms for monitoring
    critical infrastructure SCADA/ICS networks, identifying 12 previously undetected probing cam-
   paigns against energy sector assets

• Created interactive dashboards and visualization tools using D3.js and Kibana for real-time
   monitoring of global cyber threat landscape, adopted as standard analytical tooling by the
  NSA Threat Operations Center

• Implemented diﬀerential privacy mechanisms for cross-agency data sharing initiatives, enabling
   collaborative analytics on sensitive datasets while maintaining compliance with EO 12333 and
   PPD-28 privacy protections

• Authored the NSA Data Science Tradecraft Manual (112 pages), establishing standards for

Marcus T. Williams                                                         Page 3



    reproducibility, peer review, and model validation in intelligence production, now mandated for
    all NSA data science products

• Conducted peer review and technical validation of 40+ analytical products per quarter, ensuring
    statistical rigor and methodological soundness prior to dissemination to intelligence consumers

• Developed transfer learning approaches for malware classiﬁcation that reduced labeled training
   data requirements by 75% while maintaining F1 scores above 0.92 across 14 malware families

• Collaborated with DARPA program managers on the Cyber Grand Challenge follow-on research,
   contributing novel reinforcement learning approaches to automated vulnerability discovery

• Maintained and operated analytical tools on TS/SCI networks (JWICS, NSANet), ensuring
   compliance with security protocols and obtaining Authority to Operate (ATO) for 3 custom
    analytical platforms

• Received commendation from the Director of NSA for contributions to Operation GLOWING
  SYMPHONY analysis (speciﬁc details classiﬁed)

Mathematical Statistician

Grade/Series: GS-12/1529                Hours per Week: 40
Salary: $86,335 per annum                   Dates: 08/2014 – 05/2017
Employer: U.S. Census Bureau, Center for Statistical Research and Methodology
Address: 4600 Silver Hill Road, Suitland, MD 20746
Supervisor: Dr. Patricia Huang, (301) 555-9817 (may be contacted)

• Developed small area estimation models for the American Community Survey (ACS), improving
   poverty rate estimates for 650+ counties with populations under 20,000 by reducing coeﬃcient
    of variation from 28% to 14%

• Implemented record linkage algorithms using probabilistic matching (Fellegi-Sunter framework)
   to integrate administrative records from IRS, SSA, and HUD with Census survey data, achieving
   99.2% match accuracy on a corpus of 140M records

• Designed and conducted Monte Carlo simulation studies evaluating the statistical properties
    of proposed disclosure avoidance methods for the 2020 Census, contributing to the selection of
    diﬀerential privacy as the primary protection mechanism

• Built automated data quality assessment pipelines processing 3.2M survey responses monthly,
   ﬂagging anomalies and potential fabrication with 96% sensitivity, reducing ﬁeld veriﬁcation
    costs by $4.8M annually

• Authored 3 peer-reviewed publications in the Journal of the American Statistical Association
   and Survey Methodology on hierarchical Bayesian methods for multi-level survey estimation

• Contributed to the development of the Census Bureau’s Disclosure Avoidance System (DAS)
   based on zero-concentrated diﬀerential privacy, performing utility-privacy tradeoﬀanalyses for
   47 data products

• Presented research at the Joint Statistical Meetings (JSM), Federal Committee on Statistical
   Methodology (FCSM), and the Census Scientiﬁc Advisory Committee

• Developed R packages for internal use by 45+ statisticians: ceslink for entity resolution and
   saepy for small area estimation, reducing analyst setup time from days to hours

• Served on the Technical Review Panel for the Supplemental Poverty Measure, evaluating method-
    ological proposals from academic researchers and providing recommendations to the Chief Statis-
    tician

• Trained 12 new Mathematical Statisticians (GS-9/11) in Bayesian methods, R programming,

   and Census Bureau disclosure review procedures through a structured 8-week onboarding cur-
   riculum

Data Analyst (Pathways Recent Graduate)

Grade/Series: GS-9/1560                 Hours per Week: 40
Salary: $62,107 per annum                   Dates: 09/2012 – 07/2014
Employer: Department of Homeland Security, Oﬃce of Intelligence and Analysis (I&A)
Address: Nebraska Avenue Complex, Washington, DC 20528
Supervisor: Robert M. Chen, (202) 555-3892 (no longer available; HR contact provided)

• Performed quantitative analysis of suspicious activity reports (SARs) and intelligence informa-
   tion reports (IIRs) from state and local fusion centers, identifying statistical patterns indicative
    of pre-operational terrorist planning

• Developed SQL queries and Python scripts to extract, transform, and analyze data from the
   Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN), Guardian database, and eGuardian system,
   processing 150,000+ reports annually

• Created geospatial visualizations and heat maps of threat indicators using ArcGIS and Python
   (geopandas), supporting the production of 24 Homeland Intelligence Today brieﬁngs for DHS
    senior leadership

• Built predictive models for border crossing volume forecasting using ARIMA and Prophet time
    series methods, improving CBP staﬃng allocation accuracy by 18% at 12 ports of entry

• Supported the Homeland Threat Assessment production cycle by providing statistical analysis of
   threat trends, contributing data-driven assessments to the DHS Secretary’s morning intelligence
   brieﬁng

• Conducted link analysis on ﬁnancial transaction networks to identify potential terrorism ﬁnanc-
   ing pathways, resulting in 3 referrals to the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force

• Maintained databases and analytical tools on the SIPR and JWICS networks, ensuring data
    integrity and compliance with Intelligence Community standards for information handling

• Completed the DHS Intelligence Enterprise Analyst Development Program (18 months), receiv-
   ing certiﬁcation in all-source intelligence analysis and structured analytic techniques

• Collaborated with analysts from CBP, ICE HSI, and USCG Intelligence on multi-agency threat
   products, contributing statistical rigor to qualitative assessments

• Received the DHS Secretary’s Award for Excellence for contributions to the Southwest Border
    Intelligence Campaign analytics initiative
